Risk. This investment involves significant risk and is suitable only for investors of substantial net worth who can bear the complete loss of their investment and who do not need immediate cash returns. See "Risk Factors". No offer where unlawful. This document is not an offer or solicitation in any jurisdiction where such offer would be unlawful, or to anyone who has not completed a Subscription Agreement satisfactory to the Fund. The Fund may reject any subscription in whole or part and may amend the terms of the offering.

Reliance. Investors may rely only on this document (including amendments and supplements) and written answers supplied by the Fund on request. Delivery of this document does not imply that information is correct as of any later date. Tax and legal advice. Prospective investors should consult their own legal, tax and financial advisors about the consequences of acquiring, holding and disposing of Shares under the laws of their citizenship, residence and domicile.

Selling restrictions. Distribution of this document and the offering of Shares may be restricted in certain jurisdictions. Persons receiving it must inform themselves of and observe all applicable restrictions. Sample legends for common regimes (each fictional here) would address: public-offer prohibitions; limitation to professional or institutional investors; absence of local regulator review; unavailability of local investor-compensation schemes; and exemptions relied on for private placement. The Fund The Fund was incorporated on 15 February 2030 as a public company with limited liability under the laws of Zandria and is registered as a collective investment scheme with the ZFSA. It is an open-ended fund, issues Shares in classes and series, and primarily invests in securities of Veridian companies. Currently only Class A Shares are offered. The Investment Manager may establish Alternate Investment Vehicles (feeders or parallel structures) to address tax or regulatory issues of particular investors.

The Fund will seek registration as a broad-based sub-account of the Sponsor under the Veridian FII Regulations. Investment Rationale Veridia offers a large, young population, rising domestic consumption, heavy infrastructure spending and a deep, liquid equity market with thousands of listed companies. The Fund believes equity is an appropriate asset class to capture this growth and that small and mid- sized companies, often overlooked by institutions with shorter horizons, offer attractive opportunities. (Illustrative statements; no statistic here is real.)

Investment Objective The Fund is absolute-return oriented with a long bias, seeking long-term capital appreciation by investing directly or indirectly in equity-related instruments of Veridian companies. It may use long and short positions, stock and index futures and options, depositary receipts, pre-IPO investments, and securities borrowing and lending, in line with regulation.

During the Initial Offer Period up to 5,000,000 Class A Shares are offered at USD 100 each (up
to USD 500 million). The Board may increase the size by USD 500 million but the Fund will not
exceed USD 1 billion. Minimum subscription is USD 250,000, which the Board may waive.

Investment Process Opportunities are sourced through research, company visits and industry contacts and evaluated on fundamental, operational, managerial and valuation criteria. The Advisor uses discounted cash flow, comparable-company and financial-statement analysis, and focuses on absolute rather than relative performance. Positions are exited when valuation gaps close, growth-adjusted multiples look excessive, returns on capital decline, or management under- delivers. Risk Management

Risk controls cover (1) research-driven, diversified positions; (2) consistent valuation
discipline; (3) concentration limits by security, sector and market capitalization; and (4) net
long exposure between 25% and 75%. For example, a 25% net long exposure could be 62.5%
long and 37.5% short.

section: IV. Investment Objective, Approach and Risk Management
text: Investment Objective Absolute-return oriented long-term capital appreciation through investment, directly or indirectly, in equity and equity-related instruments of Veridian companies, including those listed outside Veridia. Instruments include stock and index futures (long/short), options (including covered calls and puts), depositary receipts, IPOs and securities borrowing and lending. The Fund will operate as a sub-account of the Sponsor under the Veridian FII Regulations. Investment Approach Growth at reasonable valuations; long bias; the Fund is not expected to be net short overall. Focus and prudence: invest only where the Manager believes it has an edge and reduce positions as fundamentals deteriorate. Market-cap agnostic, with a cap on small- and mid-cap exposure.

section: IV. Investment Objective, Approach and Risk Management
text: Rigorous bottom-up research on every holding, with macro trends as a secondary input. About 30–50 holdings diversified across industries. Some securities may be illiquid, which can limit the Fund's ability to exit positions or realize valuations. The Fund may use covered options, straddles, arbitrage between securities of one issuer or different issuers, and cash or money-market instruments when appropriate. If the Manager materially changes the investment objective or strategy it will give written notice and Shareholders may redeem without regard to any lock-up or redemption fees.

Shares are redeemable at the Shareholder's option on any Dealing Day after the Lock-up Period, at the quarterly Dealing Days, on at least 45 Business Days' written notice, at the Net Asset Value on the Valuation Day. The Board may permit redemptions during the lock-up. Minimum residual holding: the Shareholder must continue to hold Shares of at least USD 5,000 (variable by the Board); otherwise the Board may redeem the remainder.

10% gate: if redemptions on a day equal or exceed 10% of issued Class A Shares, the
Board may scale requests back pro rata, carrying the excess to later days with priority.

Faxed requests: valid only if the signed original is received before the Dealing Day and the Administrator confirms receipt in writing within five Business Days. Irrevocability: a request, once given, is irrevocable unless the Board determines otherwise. Settlement: in USD, normally within 14 Business Days after the Dealing Day, by direct transfer at the Shareholder's risk and cost. Compulsory redemption: the Board may redeem Shares of ineligible holders, holders in breach of law or causing regulatory or tax issues, holders below the Minimum Holding (30 days' notice to top up), and all Shares if net assets fall below USD 5 million for three consecutive months.

Consolidation: on crystallization, series that bore a Performance Profit Allocation are normally consolidated into the oldest such series, with the Reference Price reset. Anti-money laundering: redemptions may be refused or delayed pending information and are never paid to third-party accounts.

Net Asset Value is determined by the Investment Manager (delegated to the Administrator) at each Valuation Day as total assets less total liabilities, and per-share values are rounded to four decimals. Valuation principles include: 1. Cash, deposits and receivables at face value unless the Board decides otherwise.

2. Listed securities at last traded price on the principal exchange (or mean of bid and ask if none), with fair-value discretion for the Board. 3. Managed funds at last published net asset value or redemption price. 4. Unlisted or illiquid securities at fair value determined by the Board or Manager having regard to cost, recent transactions, holding size and other factors. 5. Exchange-traded and OTC derivatives by reference to official settlement prices or counterparty valuations. 6. Non-USD amounts converted at rates the Board deems appropriate. 7. Securities not traded on a Valuation Day valued at the last trade within thirty days.

Each Class or series has its own Class Account; changes in portfolio value are allocated pro rata by prior Net Asset Value, with designated Class Adjustments (for example currency hedging costs) applied to the relevant Class.
Initial Fee. As in the Definitions. Management Fee. 2% per annum of Class A Net Asset Value (before that month's fee and any accrued Performance Profit Allocation), payable monthly in arrears.

Performance Profit Allocation. Calculated share by share so that only appreciating series bear it. At each year-end (or on redemption), it equals 20% of the positive difference between the series' Net Asset Value per Share (before current-year performance and Management Fees) and the Reference Price, subject to the High Water Mark. On crystallization the High Water Mark resets to the post-allocation Net Asset Value. It is paid to Class B Shareholders by dividend or redemption proceeds within 30 days of the Performance Period end. Secondary transfers during a Performance Period are treated as a redemption by the transferor. Investment Advisor's Fee. Paid by the Investment Manager. Administrator and Secretary. Approximately USD 45,000 per annum, plus fees for Zandrian tax filings.

Risks of investing in Veridia and Veridian companies. Political, social and economic instability; regional tensions; reliance on agriculture; differing accounting standards; evolving securities regulation; competition and capital needs.

Stock market volatility and smaller companies. Thin trading, wider price swings, limited resources and higher transaction costs. Reliance on the tax treaty. The treaty may be renegotiated or terminated, or tax authorities may deny benefits. Limitations on investments. Ownership limits on sub-accounts and caps on debt securities. Multinational litigation. Difficulty joining parties and enforcing judgments. Investment and repatriation restrictions. Approvals and withholding taxes may apply and rules may tighten. Regulatory status. The Manager is not registered as an investment adviser; no separate counsel for the Fund or investors; regulators may adopt additional hedge-fund regulation. Activities of the Investment Manager. Not required to devote full time; other portfolios; inside-information trading restrictions; trade aggregation. New investors and dilution.

Non-transferability and limited redemption rights. Transfers need Fund consent; redemptions only quarterly after lock-up. Tax considerations and permanent establishment exposure. Withholding may change; authorities may assert a permanent establishment, jeopardizing treaty benefits.
The following is a fictional illustration of how a taxation section is structured. It does not describe any real tax law.

Investors should consult their own advisors on the consequences of subscribing for, holding and redeeming Shares in their country of citizenship, residence or domicile. Zandria The Fund holds a Category 1 Global Business Licence and is taxed at 15% on net income, with a deemed foreign-tax credit equal to the higher of actual foreign tax and 80% of Zandrian tax on foreign-source income (an effective 3%). There is no capital gains tax and no withholding tax on dividends or redemption proceeds. A tax residency certificate, renewed annually, depends on central management and control being demonstrably in Zandria. Veridia Subject to the treaty and the Fund having no permanent establishment: Capital gains on Veridian securities are not taxed in Veridia.

Dividends are exempt in shareholders' hands (the distributing company bears distribution tax). Interest income is taxed at 20% (10% on certain convertible bonds). If treaty benefits are unavailable or a permanent establishment exists, short-term gains on listed securities may be taxed at 15%, long-term gains may be exempt subject to securities transaction tax and a 10% minimum alternate tax, and other gains at higher rates. Securities transaction tax applies to dealings on Veridian exchanges at rates between roughly 0.017% and 0.25%, depending on the transaction type.

Fictional illustration of structure only. Zandria Exchange controls: none in force. Regulatory: the Fund qualifies as an investment company, is authorised as a collective investment scheme under the Zandria Securities Act, and operates under a Category 1 Global Business Licence subject to an annual fee and penalties for late payment. Anti-money laundering: under the national AML statute and code, the registrar verifies identity, source of funds and the legitimacy of subscription monies; failure to provide information permits refusal of applications or redemptions; redemption proceeds are never paid to third-party accounts. Veridia FII framework: FIIs may invest in listed and unlisted shares, debentures and warrants, mutual fund units, government securities, exchange-traded derivatives, commercial

paper and similar instruments, and may register sub-accounts. A broad-based sub-
account must have at least 20 investors with none holding more than 49%.

Ownership limits: aggregate FII holding in a company is capped (24%, raisable by shareholder resolution); a single FII or broad-based sub-account may hold up to 10% (5% for corporate or individual sub-accounts); equity-related investments must be at least 70% of an FII's portfolio unless registered as a debt fund. Participatory notes and offshore derivatives: monthly disclosure to the regulator; restrictions on issuance by sub-accounts and a wind-down period for derivative-linked instruments. Public offerings and takeovers: disclosure guidelines and takeover regulations may affect entry and exit; thresholds trigger notification to the company and exchanges. Exchange controls: the central bank authorises foreign-currency and special non- resident rupee-type accounts for three years, renewable; proceeds may be repatriated after taxes.

Anti-money laundering: transaction records above a threshold, a principal officer, suspicious-transaction reporting, and investor consent to disclosure to regulators and the financial intelligence unit.
